headline: Japan Digital Agency survey reports self-reported time savings and uneven uptake for government AI Gennai
summary: Japan’s Digital Agency published the first usage survey for Gennai, its government generative-AI environment. The questionnaire received 6,439 responses from government employees across ministries and related bodies; the satisfaction and task-time results reported here use a 3,078-person subset. The Agency reports 71.7% satisfaction in that subset and estimates about 1.83 hours saved per user per week from self-reported task-time bands. Its materials differ slightly on the share reporting at least one hour saved: 54.4% on the release page and detailed PDF page, versus 54.5% on the PDF overview slide. The estimate uses band midpoints, caps “10+ hours saved” at 10, and treats unknown/no-change responses as zero. About 31.2% of all 6,439 respondents said they rarely or never used Gennai. These are first-party survey responses and an assumption-based estimate, not independently measured time savings or causal evidence.
